Oncology/oncogenic subtyping domains apply; SHAP is excluded as an explainability method.

The paper trains epigenetic aging clocks on rat RRBS methylation data to estimate organ-specific age acceleration, a supervised regression approach (classically penalized regression). The domain is epigenetics/aging research in a selectively bred rat model.

model_type: ["kernel principal component analysis", "principal component analysis", "level set method"]
rationale: The paper fits Kernel PCA on training shapes to build a shape prior for level-set segmentation, an unsupervised statistical learning step, so the model is trained in this study. The domain is computer vision (CVPR) with imaging and machine learning as key areas; no biomedical application is stated in the abstract.

The paper develops a fuzzy rule-based decision fusion framework combining two classical signal-detection methods (peak picking and template matching) for supervised P300 detection in EEG-based BCI; SVM appears only as a performance comparator and is therefore excluded.

The paper trains a self-supervised voxel embedding model (UAE) with prototypical contrastive loss for anatomical landmark matching, so it is a self-supervised representation-learning method. The abstract names no specific neural architecture, so only the model's own name is tagged and the domain centres on medical image analysis and machine learning.

The paper proposes and trains a hybrid of self-feedback neural networks and generalized regression neural networks for associative pattern recall, using a new one-shot learning algorithm; both are shallow, non-deep neural architectures, so 'classic neural network' is the appropriate family. As biomedical-vocabulary fields are largely irrelevant, the domain is computer science / machine learning.

The paper trains a 3D nnU-Net (a CNN-based segmentation architecture) on hip cartilage MRI, with uncertainty derived from ensembled sub-networks, and trains a logistic model to combine uncertainty and sensitivity scores for error localisation. Domain centres on musculoskeletal MRI segmentation, i.e. medical imaging applied to musculoskeletal medicine.

The paper trains prediction models on sensor and simulated time-series data to forecast psychological symptoms, so the models are trained in-study under a supervised paradigm. Its methodological contribution centres on 'super learning' approaches and averaging predictions across training windows, i.e. stacking/ensemble methods, with no specific base algorithms named in the abstract.

A recurrent neural network is trained on sentence-situation pairs from a microworld to demonstrate systematicity in sentence comprehension, i.e., supervised training of the model within this study. The work is a computational/connectionist modelling study of language processing, best captured under Computer science with Machine learning and Natural language processing.

The paper trains a support vector machine variant (Fisher-kernel style) whose kernel is derived from a hidden Markov model of protein families, both of which are classical (non-neural) statistical learning methods used in a supervised classification task over SCOP superfamilies. The subject is computational biology applied to protein sequence homology detection.

The paper trains Top-Scoring Pair (TSP) classifiers on gene expression profiles to diagnose and predict human diseases, a non-neural supervised classification method, hence classical machine learning. The subject is gene-expression-based disease classification, placing it in genomics/medical informatics with gene expression and phenotype classification as core tier-3 topics.

The paper develops and fits radial basis function networks (a shallow neural architecture) to approximate inverse continuous time variant functions using a damped least-squares training solution, so it is supervised training of a classic neural network. The subject is mathematical function computation via neural methods rather than any biomedical application, giving computer science with machine learning and applied mathematics as sub-domains.

The paper performs a genetic association study in heart failure patients undergoing CRT and trains supervised rule induction algorithms to classify responders vs nonresponders from genetic variants and clinical parameters. Domain tagging centers on cardiology and genetic variation; the only named model is the rule induction classifier, a classical ML approach trained on the study's own data.

OncoGAN is a generative model trained in this study (unsupervised) that combines GANs and variational autoencoders to synthesize cancer genomes, while DeepTumour is an existing deep learning tool applied as-is for validation and augmented-training experiments. The domain is cancer genomics focused on somatic mutations, copy number alterations and structural variants in whole-genome data.

The paper proposes and trains the UST-RUN segmentation framework for a new mixed-domain semi-supervised setting, learning from a small labelled set plus unlabelled multi-domain data via pseudo-labels (semi-supervised). No concrete model architecture (e.g. CNN/transformer) is named in the abstract, so no model_family can be assigned; components like copy-paste and MixUp are data augmentation techniques, not model types.

The paper trains a multi-omics prognosis model on TCGA data, using a VAE (and PCC-based integration) for unsupervised multi-modal integration and a domain-adaptation transfer learning scheme pre-trained on the majority group and fine-tuned on the minority group for supervised PFI prediction. SMOTE is a data augmentation technique, not a model, and the subject is prostate cancer health-disparities research driven by multi-omics ML.

Mass-spectral proteomics biomarker classification with supervised models trained on labelled spectra; MLP is a shallow neural net (classic neural network) and naive Bayes is classical ML. Six other induction algorithms are mentioned but unnamed, so they are not tagged.

The paper proposes a transductive-inference framework for estimating diagnosis reliability and evaluates it on UCI medical datasets and coronary artery disease diagnosis, but the abstract names no specific ML algorithm or architecture, so model_type and model_family are left empty. Models are fit on labelled medical datasets (supervised), with the transductive procedure serving as a reliability-estimation wrapper rather than a distinct second learning step.

The paper trains a collective matrix factorization model to transfer link-prediction knowledge from a dense source PPI network (human) to a sparse target network (H. pylori), using observed interactions as supervision. Domain-wise it is a computational biology/bioinformatics study of protein-protein interaction prediction.

The study applies the previously developed, clinical-grade mRNA-based immune classifier ImPrint (ImPrint+/ImPrint- stratification) to predict pCR in HR+HER2- breast cancer patients from I-SPY2, with no training or fine-tuning performed in this paper. Domains reflect the oncology/immunotherapy biomarker context of an mRNA expression-based predictive assay.

The study trains a linear SVM for supervised classification and variational Bayesian Gaussian mixture models for unsupervised clustering on DCM-derived features from fMRI, so both paradigms apply with classical ML families. DCM itself is a dynamical-systems generative model used for feature construction, not one of the paper's machine-learning models.

The paper trains a supervised disease-prediction model based on differential expression pairs from blood RNA data to detect liver cancer, compared against an alternative classifier built in Weka. The subject is blood transcriptomic gene-expression signature discovery for cancer diagnostics, so omics/transcriptomics and biomarker/oncology domains apply.

The paper trains Random Forest models on a 300K SNP multiple sclerosis case-control GWAS dataset to discover disease-associated variants, a supervised classical ML ensemble application. The subject is genetic association analysis of human disease, warranting GWAS/genetics domain terms.

The pretrained SSL vision foundation models Prov-GigaPath and UNI were applied as-is to extract whole-slide-image embeddings, while slide-level classifiers were trained on those embeddings in a supervised manner for steatosis classification. The domain is pathology/digital imaging of liver donor biopsies for transplant decision-making.

The paper trains a multiomics predictive model with machine learning algorithms on labelled treatment-outcome data, so it is supervised and trained in this study; however, the abstract names no specific algorithm or model family, so model_type and model_family remain empty. Domains reflect the clinical oncology focus integrating metagenomic, metaproteomic and metabolomic profiling of fecal samples.

The paper proposes and trains structural Laplacian eigenmaps, a non-neural unsupervised manifold-learning/dimensionality-reduction method, whose resulting embeddings are then used for classification in computer-vision applications (action recognition, human interaction classification). No biomedical domain terms are warranted beyond the general CS/ML framing, and no deep, ensemble, or generative components are described.

The abstract reports that machine learning was used to characterize acoustic profiles of vocalizations but names no algorithm, model family, or learning paradigm, so model_type and model_family are left empty. The subject is human emotional perception and vocal communication (human biology), with machine learning as an applied method.

The paper trains a semi-supervised segmentation framework (UC-Seg) from scratch using consistency regularization and uncertainty-guided pseudo-labelling on MRI, CT, ultrasound and colonoscopy images. The abstract names no concrete architecture or algorithm for its subnets (only the mean-teacher baseline is mentioned as context), so model_type and model_family are left empty.

The abstract describes novel machine learning models trained on their own data (with molecular dynamics simulations and validation experiments) to predict stabilizing interactions in viral fusion protein gB, implying a supervised predictive task, but names no specific algorithm, so model_type and model_family remain empty per the evidence rules. Domain tags reflect structural virology combining simulation and ML modeling of protein interactions.

The paper contributes a billion-scale proteomics (MS/MS) dataset and trains XuanjiNovo, a non-autoregressive Transformer, on 100 million PSMs to infer peptide sequences from spectra; curriculum learning is a training technique, not a model type. The supervised paradigm applies since spectra are trained against known peptide labels (PSMs).

The paper trains a VAE to learn a latent representation of heart rate response curves (unsupervised), then clusters in the latent space and applies the pre-trained autoencoder to an external fear-conditioning dataset. A generative deep model learning latent representations maps to deep learning, generative AI, and representation learning; the clustering algorithm itself is not specifically named beyond 'cluster analysis'.

The paper develops and fits a novel non-uniform MRF probabilistic model with pivotal/non-pivotal control points for non-rigid DSA image registration, with no labeled learning involved, so the MRF is optimized directly on the paper's clinical image data. The subject is a computational registration algorithm applied to medical imaging, hence the computer science/imaging domain terms.

A pure computer-vision/pattern-recognition paper (IEEE TPAMI) with no biomedical content, so domains are tagged at the computer science / machine learning level only. The authors develop and estimate the eigen light-field (an eigenfaces-style eigendecomposition used as features for face recognition across pose), giving an unsupervised dimensionality-reduction-type model trained on their own image data.

model_type: ["segmentation foundation model", "training-free ensemble fusion", "multi-source knowledge distillation student model"]
rationale: The paper benchmarks six pretrained segmentation foundation models as-is on organ segmentation and additionally trains synergistic models via training-free fusion and multi-source knowledge distillation, whose teacher-generated labels on unlabelled scans constitute pseudo-labelling (semi-supervised). Domains reflect medical image segmentation; knowledge distillation and fusion are captured as the synergy paradigm with deep learning and ensemble learning as families.
